[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/21 (Sun) 20:04  
[FACT] User has been trying to improve skills in data science and programming over the past month.  
[PREFERENCE] User is looking for recommendations on books about machine learning.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended books for machine learning:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "Machine Learning" by Tom Mitchell: A classic introduction covering supervised and unsupervised learning, linear regression, decision trees, and neural networks.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "Python Machine Learning" by Sebastian Raschka: A hands-on guide covering scikit-learn, TensorFlow, and Keras.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras, and TensorFlow" by Aurélien Géron: A practical guide focusing on scikit-learn, Keras, and TensorFlow.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "Deep Learning" by Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio, and Aaron Courville: A comprehensive book on deep learning covering neural networks, convolutional networks, and recurrent networks.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning" by Christopher Bishop: A mathematical introduction covering probability theory, linear algebra, and optimization techniques.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "Machine Learning Yearning" by Andrew Ng: Focuses on practical aspects of machine learning, including data preparation and model selection.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction" by Richard S. Sutton and Andrew G. Barto: Comprehensive coverage of reinforcement learning.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "Deep Reinforcement Learning" by Mnih et al.: Focuses on deep learning and reinforcement learning intersection.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] "Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning" by Carl Edward Rasmussen and Christopher K. I. Williams: Covers Gaussian processes in Bayesian machine learning.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Other recommendations include "Introduction to Machine Learning" by Ethem Alpaydin, "Machine Learning for Hackers" by Danny B. Lange, and "Building Intelligent Systems: A Guide to Machine Learning Engineering" by Chandan K. Reddy and Vikramaditya Jakkula.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Emphasized that practice is key to mastering machine learning and suggested working on projects and participating in Kaggle competitions.  
[PREFERENCE] User is particularly interested in deep learning and plans to start with "Deep Learning" by Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio, and Aaron Courville.  
[FACT] User has been watching video lectures on statistics by Professor Andrew Ng on MIT OpenCourseWare.
